sections.title: Advanced Concept
sections.content: Level 2 includes problems with multiple workers of different efficiencies, fractional work, sequential tasks, pipes & cistern, and wages-based distribution. Each worker may have a different efficiency, requiring logical setup.

sections.title: Efficiency
sections.content:
Efficiency = 1 / Time (days). If worker A is d times faster than worker B, then efficiency of A = d × efficiency of B.
Example: Mohan completes work in 5 days, Reena works 2× faster, so Reena's efficiency = 2 × 1/5 = 2/5 per day.

sections.title: Combined Work
sections.content: Combined work rate = sum of all individual rates. Time = total work ÷ combined rate.

sections.title: Fractional Work
sections.content:
If part of the work is done initially, remaining time = remaining work ÷ combined rate.
Example: Total work = 1, first day 1/4 done, rate = 1/2 per day, remaining time = (1-1/4)/(1/2) = 1.5 days.

sections.title: Sequential Work
sections.content: If workers start at different times, calculate work done in each segment: Time × Rate = Partial Work. Total work = sum of all partial works.

sections.title: Pipes & Cistern Variation
sections.content: Filling pipe rate = 1 / filling time, Emptying pipe rate = 1 / emptying time (negative). Net rate = filling rate - empty rate. Time = total work ÷ net rate. Consider fractional filling/emptying carefully.

sections.title: Wages & Work Linkage
sections.content: Wages ∝ work done. Individual share = individual work ÷ total work × total wages. If efficiency differs, share = individual rate × time segment.

sections.title: Important Formulas
sections.content:
1. Efficiency = 1 / Time
2. Combined rate = sum of individual efficiencies
3. Fractional work: Remaining ÷ rate
4. Sequential work: segment-wise calculation
5. Pipes net rate = filling rate - emptying rate
6. Wages = proportional to work done
7. Time = total work ÷ net rate

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
• Taking wrong efficiency ratio
• Not summing partial works in sequential problems
• Forgetting ± in pipes problems
• Using wrong fraction for partial work
• Ignoring proportionality in wages

sections.title: Summary
sections.content:
• Efficiency ∝ 1/Time
• Combined and sequential work: calculate segment-wise
• Fractional work: remaining ÷ rate
• Pipes: net rate = fill - empty
• Wages: proportional to work done
• Multi-step problems require logical stepwise solving

tricks.title: Multiple Worker Rate Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Add all workers' rates, then total work ÷ combined rate = total time

tricks.title: Sequential Work Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Calculate partial work for each segment, sum them, total work = 1
tricks.example: A 2 days, B 3 days, segment-wise sum gives total work=1

tricks.title: Fractional Work Trick
tricks.explanation: Subtract already completed fraction, then divide by rate

tricks.title: Pipes & Cistern Trick
tricks.explanation: Net rate = fill rate - empty rate, Time = total ÷ net
tricks.example: Fill 6 days, empty 12 days, Net rate=1/6-1/12=1/12, Time=12 days

tricks.title: Efficiency Ratio Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Faster worker rate = ratio × slower worker rate

tricks.title: Wages Quick Share
tricks.explanation: Individual share = individual work ÷ total work × total wages

tricks.title: Alternate Day Work Trick
tricks.explanation: For alternating workers, sum partial works day by day until total=1
tricks.example: A,B alternate, Day1 A 1/4, Day2 B 1/5, sum until total work=1

tricks.title: Multi-step Efficiency Tip
tricks.explanation: Solve each segment stepwise, then sum partial works
tricks.example: Day1 A+B, Day2 B+C, Total work=sum of all partial works
